questions.q: During the electrolysis of a certain aqueous salt solution using inert platinum electrodes, it is observed that the pH of the solution increases in the space near the cathode and decreases in the space near the anode. Which of the following salt solutions was electrolysed?
questions.question: During the electrolysis of a certain aqueous salt solution using inert platinum electrodes, it is observed that the pH of the solution increases in the space near the cathode and decreases in the space near the anode. Which of the following salt solutions was electrolysed?
questions.solution:
During the electrolysis of aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ using inert platinum electrodes, the following reactions occur at the electrodes:

At the cathode, water is reduced instead of $\text{Na}^+$ ions because the standard reduction potential of water is higher than that of $\text{Na}^+$:
$2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2(g) + 2\text{OH}^-(aq)$
The production of $\text{OH}^-$ ions increases the concentration of hydroxide ions in the space near the cathode, leading to an increase in pH.

At the anode, water is oxidized instead of $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions because the standard oxidation potential of water is higher than that of $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$:
$2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 4e^-$
The production of $\text{H}^+$ ions increases the concentration of hydrogen ions in the space near the anode, leading to a decrease in pH.

For concentrated aqueous $\text{NaCl}$, $\text{Cl}^-$ is oxidized at the anode, so the pH does not decrease significantly near the anode. For aqueous $\text{CuSO}_4$ and $\text{AgNO}_3$, metal ions are reduced at the cathode, so the pH does not increase near the cathode.

Answer: Aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two electrolytic cells, one containing an aqueous solution of acidified ferrous chloride ($\text{FeCl}_2$) and the other containing an aqueous solution of acidified ferric chloride ($\text{FeCl}_3$), are connected in series. A constant direct current is passed through both cells for a given duration. Assuming complete reduction to iron metal at the cathodes and 100% current efficiency, the ratio of the mass of iron deposited in the first cell to that deposited in the second cell is $x : 2$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.question: Two electrolytic cells, one containing an aqueous solution of acidified ferrous chloride ($\text{FeCl}_2$) and the other containing an aqueous solution of acidified ferric chloride ($\text{FeCl}_3$), are connected in series. A constant direct current is passed through both cells for a given duration. Assuming complete reduction to iron metal at the cathodes and 100% current efficiency, the ratio of the mass of iron deposited in the first cell to that deposited in the second cell is $x : 2$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's second law of electrolysis, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different cells connected in series, the mass of the substance deposited at the electrodes is directly proportional to its equivalent weight.

The equivalent weight of a substance is given by $E = \dfrac{M}{n}$, where $M$ is the molar mass and $n$ is the number of electrons involved in the reduction half-reaction.

For the first cell containing $\text{FeCl}_2$, iron is in the $+2$ oxidation state. The reduction reaction is $\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Fe}$.
Equivalent weight of iron in the first cell, $E_1 = \dfrac{M}{2}$.

For the second cell containing $\text{FeCl}_3$, iron is in the $+3$ oxidation state. The reduction reaction is $\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Fe}$.
Equivalent weight of iron in the second cell, $E_2 = \dfrac{M}{3}$.

The ratio of the mass of iron deposited in the first cell ($m_1$) to that in the second cell ($m_2$) is equal to the ratio of their equivalent weights:

$\dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac{E_1}{E_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{M}{2}}{\dfrac{M}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Given that the ratio is $x : 2$, we get $x = 3$.

Answer: $3$

questions.q:
A galvanic cell is constructed by combining an aluminium electrode (weighing $50 \text{ g}$) immersed in an $\text{Al}^{3+}$ solution and a copper electrode immersed in $2.0 \text{ L}$ of a $1.0 \text{ M}$ aqueous solution of $\text{CuSO}_4$. The cell delivers a steady current of $2.0 \text{ A}$. Assuming the cell operates ideally until one of the active reactants is completely consumed, the maximum operating time of the cell is ________ hours. (Nearest integer)

[Given: Molar mass of $\text{Al} = 27 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$]
questions.question:
A galvanic cell is constructed by combining an aluminium electrode (weighing $50 \text{ g}$) immersed in an $\text{Al}^{3+}$ solution and a copper electrode immersed in $2.0 \text{ L}$ of a $1.0 \text{ M}$ aqueous solution of $\text{CuSO}_4$. The cell delivers a steady current of $2.0 \text{ A}$. Assuming the cell operates ideally until one of the active reactants is completely consumed, the maximum operating time of the cell is ________ hours. (Nearest integer)

[Given: Molar mass of $\text{Al} = 27 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
The cell reactions are:

Anode: $\text{Al} \rightarrow \text{Al}^{3+} + 3\text{e}^{-}$

Cathode: $\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^{-} \rightarrow \text{Cu}$

Moles of $\text{Al}$ available $= \dfrac{50}{27} \approx 1.85 \text{ mol}$

Moles of electrons that can be provided by $\text{Al} = 3 \times \dfrac{50}{27} \approx 5.55 \text{ mol}$

Moles of $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ available $= 2.0 \text{ L} \times 1.0 \text{ M} = 2.0 \text{ mol}$

Moles of electrons that can be consumed by $\text{Cu}^{2+} = 2 \times 2.0 = 4.0 \text{ mol}$

Since $4.0 < 5.55$, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ is the limiting reactant.

Total charge $Q = n \times F = 4.0 \times 96500 = 386000 \text{ C}$

Using $Q = I \times t$, the time $t$ in seconds is:

$t = \dfrac{Q}{I} = \dfrac{386000}{2.0} = 193000 \text{ s}$

Converting time to hours:

$t = \dfrac{193000}{3600} \approx 53.61 \text{ hours}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the maximum operating time is $54$ hours.

Answer: $54$

Mass of $\text{Ag}$ deposited = $0.05 \times 108 = 5.4 \text{ g}$

Given that the mass of silver deposited is $x \times 10^{-1} \text{ g}$, we have:

$x \times 10^{-1} = 5.4$

$x = 54$

The mass of $\text{Pb}$ consumed when the battery delivers a steady current of $2.5 \text{ A}$ for $20 \text{ hours}$ is _______ $\text{g}$. (Nearest integer)

Moles of $\text{Pb}$ consumed, $n_{\text{Pb}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times n_e = \dfrac{180}{193} \text{ mol}$

Mass of $\text{Pb}$ consumed $= n_{\text{Pb}} \times \text{Molar mass of Pb}$

Mass $= \dfrac{180}{193} \times 207 = \dfrac{37260}{193} \approx 193.05 \text{ g}$

The nearest integer is $193$.

Answer: $193$

An electrolytic cell containing aqueous copper(II) sulfate solution is electrolysed using a silver anode and a platinum cathode. After passing a constant current for some time, it is found that $1.27 \text{ g}$ of copper is deposited on the cathode. The loss in mass of the silver anode during this process is $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ g}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: molar masses of $\text{Cu} = 63.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ and $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
An electrolytic cell containing aqueous copper(II) sulfate solution is electrolysed using a silver anode and a platinum cathode. After passing a constant current for some time, it is found that $1.27 \text{ g}$ of copper is deposited on the cathode. The loss in mass of the silver anode during this process is $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ g}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: molar masses of $\text{Cu} = 63.5 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ and $\text{Ag} = 108 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
At the cathode, copper is deposited by the reduction of $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions:
$\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}$

Moles of copper deposited = $\dfrac{1.27}{63.5} = 0.02 \text{ mol}$

Since 2 moles of electrons are required to deposit 1 mole of Cu, the moles of electrons passed through the cell is:
$n_e = 0.02 \times 2 = 0.04 \text{ mol}$

At the anode, silver is an active electrode and undergoes oxidation:
$\text{Ag} \rightarrow \text{Ag}^+ + \text{e}^-$

Since 1 mole of electrons dissolves 1 mole of Ag, the moles of silver dissolved is equal to the moles of electrons passed:
Moles of Ag dissolved = $0.04 \text{ mol}$

Mass of silver dissolved = $0.04 \times 108 = 4.32 \text{ g}$

The loss in mass of the silver anode is given as $x \times 10^{-2} \text{ g}$.
Therefore, $4.32 = x \times 10^{-2}$
$x = 432$

Answer: $432$

questions.question: The quantity of electricity required to completely reduce $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ in acidic medium is $x\text{ F}$ (where $\text{F}$ is Faraday's constant). The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution:
The balanced half-reaction for the reduction of dichromate ion in acidic medium is given by:

$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The oxidation state of $\text{Cr}$ in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ is $+6$ and it reduces to $+3$ in $\text{Cr}^{3+}$.

The change in oxidation state per $\text{Cr}$ atom is $3$. Since there are two $\text{Cr}$ atoms in one mole of $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$, the total number of moles of electrons required for the reduction of $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ is $2 \times 3 = 6\text{ mol}$.

The quantity of electricity required is equal to the number of moles of electrons in Faradays, which is $6\text{ F}$.

Therefore, the value of $x$ is $6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.question:
Three electrolytic cells containing the electrolytes given in the table below are connected in series and a steady direct current is passed through them.
CellElectrolyteMetal ion reduced at cathode
1Molten $\text{AlCl}_3$$\text{Al}^{3+}$
2Aqueous $\text{CuSO}_4$$\text{Cu}^{2+}$
3Aqueous $\text{AgNO}_3$$\text{Ag}^{+}$

The molar ratio of the metals $\text{Al}$, $\text{Cu}$, and $\text{Ag}$ deposited at the respective cathodes is:
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's second law of electrolysis, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes connected in series, the moles of substances deposited at the electrodes are inversely proportional to the number of electrons involved in their reduction.

The reduction reactions at the cathodes are:
$\text{Al}^{3+} + 3e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Al}$
$\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Cu}$
$\text{Ag}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Ag}$

Let $Q$ Faradays of charge be passed through the cells. The number of moles of each metal deposited will be:
$n_{\text{Al}} = \dfrac{Q}{3}$
$n_{\text{Cu}} = \dfrac{Q}{2}$
$n_{\text{Ag}} = \dfrac{Q}{1}$

The molar ratio of the metals deposited is:
$n_{\text{Al}} : n_{\text{Cu}} : n_{\text{Ag}} = \dfrac{1}{3} : \dfrac{1}{2} : 1$

Multiplying by $6$ to obtain a whole number ratio:
$n_{\text{Al}} : n_{\text{Cu}} : n_{\text{Ag}} = 2 : 3 : 6$

Answer: $2 : 3 : 6$

Electrolysis of a cold concentrated aqueous solution of potassium hydrogen sulphate produces peroxodisulphate ($\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$) ions. Assuming $80\%$ current efficiency, the current required to achieve a production of $0.1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$ in $965 \text{ s}$ is ____ A.
(Given: $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
Electrolysis of a cold concentrated aqueous solution of potassium hydrogen sulphate produces peroxodisulphate ($\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$) ions. Assuming $80\%$ current efficiency, the current required to achieve a production of $0.1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$ in $965 \text{ s}$ is ____ A.
(Given: $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The oxidation reaction at the anode is:

$2\text{HSO}_4^- \rightarrow \text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^-$

To produce $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$, $2 \text{ mol}$ of electrons are required.

Moles of electrons required to produce $0.1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$ is:

$n = 0.1 \times 2 = 0.2 \text{ mol}$

The theoretical charge required is:

$Q = n \times F = 0.2 \times 96500 = 19300 \text{ C}$

Using the formula for charge with current efficiency $\eta$:

$I \times t \times \eta = Q$

$I \times 965 \times 0.80 = 19300$

$I \times 0.80 = 20$

$I = \dfrac{20}{0.80} = 25 \text{ A}$

Answer: $25$

questions.question: The number of Faradays required to produce $1$ mole of $\text{Mg}$ from molten $\text{MgCl}_2$ is ____.

The dissociation of molten $\text{MgCl}_2$ is given by:

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1$ mole of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ requires $2$ moles of electrons to produce $1$ mole of $\text{Mg}$.

Since $1$ mole of electrons corresponds to $1$ Faraday of charge, $2$ moles of electrons correspond to $2$ Faradays.

Answer: $2$

A constant current of $5\text{ A}$ is passed through a dilute aqueous solution of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ for $9650\text{ s}$ using platinum electrodes. The volume of $\text{O}_2$ gas liberated at the anode at $273\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ pressure is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ L}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: $1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$, molar volume of an ideal gas at $273\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ is $22.4\text{ L mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A constant current of $5\text{ A}$ is passed through a dilute aqueous solution of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ for $9650\text{ s}$ using platinum electrodes. The volume of $\text{O}_2$ gas liberated at the anode at $273\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ pressure is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ L}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: $1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$, molar volume of an ideal gas at $273\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ is $22.4\text{ L mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The total charge passed through the solution is given by:

$Q = I \times t$

$Q = 5 \times 9650 = 48250\text{ C}$

The number of moles of electrons (Faradays) passed is:

$n_e = \dfrac{Q}{F} = \dfrac{48250}{96500} = 0.5\text{ mol}$

During the electrolysis of dilute aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, water is oxidized at the anode to liberate $\text{O}_2$ gas. The oxidation half-reaction is:

$2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{O}_2(g) + 4\text{H}^+(aq) + 4e^-$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $4\text{ moles}$ of electrons produce $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{O}_2$ gas. Therefore, the number of moles of $\text{O}_2$ produced is:

$n_{\text{O}_2} = \dfrac{n_e}{4} = \dfrac{0.5}{4} = 0.125\text{ mol}$

The volume of $1\text{ mole}$ of an ideal gas at $273\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ is $22.4\text{ L}$. The volume of $\text{O}_2$ gas liberated is:

$V_{\text{O}_2} = n_{\text{O}_2} \times 22.4$

$V_{\text{O}_2} = 0.125 \times 22.4 = 2.8\text{ L}$

We are given that the volume is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ L}$. Equating the two values:

$x \times 10^{-1} = 2.8$

$x = 28$

Answer: $28$

(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
An electrolytic cell contains an aqueous solution of $\text{AgNO}_3$ with platinum electrodes. A direct current is passed through the cell until $2.4\text{ g}$ of $\text{O}_2$ gas is liberated at the anode. The mass of silver deposited at the cathode is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ g}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Ag} = 108\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, $\text{O} = 16\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The reaction at the anode involves the oxidation of water to oxygen gas:

$2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^-$

The reaction at the cathode involves the reduction of silver ions to silver metal:

$\text{Ag}^+ + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Ag}$

Moles of $\text{O}_2$ liberated = $\dfrac{2.4}{32} = 0.075\text{ mol}$

From the anode reaction, $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_2$ requires $4\text{ mol}$ of electrons. Therefore, the moles of electrons passed through the cell is:

$4 \times 0.075 = 0.3\text{ mol}$

From the cathode reaction, $1\text{ mol}$ of electrons deposits $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Ag}$. Thus, the moles of $\text{Ag}$ deposited is $0.3\text{ mol}$.

Mass of $\text{Ag}$ deposited = $0.3 \times 108 = 32.4\text{ g}$

Given that the mass of silver deposited is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ g}$, we have:

$x \times 10^{-1} = 32.4$

$x = 324$

Answer: $324$

When $19300 \text{ C}$ of electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of a salt of metal $\text{M}$, $4.5 \text{ g}$ of the metal is deposited at the cathode. Given that the atomic mass of $\text{M}$ is $90 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, the oxidation state of the metal cation in the salt is ____.
(Given: $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
When $19300 \text{ C}$ of electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of a salt of metal $\text{M}$, $4.5 \text{ g}$ of the metal is deposited at the cathode. Given that the atomic mass of $\text{M}$ is $90 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$, the oxidation state of the metal cation in the salt is ____.
(Given: $1 \text{ F} = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's law of electrolysis, the mass of metal deposited is given by:

$m = \dfrac{M}{nF} \times Q$

where $n$ is the oxidation state of the metal cation.

Substituting the given values:

$4.5 = \dfrac{90}{n \times 96500} \times 19300$

$4.5 = \dfrac{90}{n \times 5}$

$4.5 = \dfrac{18}{n}$

$n = \dfrac{18}{4.5} = 4$

The oxidation state of the metal cation is $4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.solution:
Given current $I = 8 \text{ A}$ and time $t = 2 \text{ minutes} = 120 \text{ s}$.

Total charge $Q$ flowing through the circuit is given by:

$n = 600 \times 10^{19} = 6 \times 10^{21}$

Comparing with $x \times 10^{21}$, we get $x = 6$.

Answer: $6$

(Given: Faraday constant $F = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)

questions.question:
A current of $10.0$ A is drawn from a Daniell cell for $1930$ s. The mass gained by the cathode during this period is $x imes 10^{-2}$ g. The value of $x$ is ____.

(Given: Faraday constant $= 96500\ \text{C mol}^{-1}$, Atomic masses: $\text{Cu} = 63.5\ \text{u}$, $\text{Zn} = 65.4\ \text{u}$)
questions.solution:
The charge passed through the Daniell cell is given by:

$Q = I \times t = 10.0 \times 1930 = 19300\ \text{C}$

Number of Faradays passed $= \dfrac{19300}{96500} = 0.2\ \text{F}$

In a Daniell cell, the cathode is made of copper. The reduction reaction at the cathode is:

$\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Cu}$

Since $2\ \text{F}$ of charge deposits $1\ \text{mol}$ of Cu, $0.2\ \text{F}$ of charge will deposit:

$\dfrac{0.2}{2} = 0.1\ \text{mol of Cu}$

Mass of Cu deposited $= 0.1 \times 63.5 = 6.35\ \text{g}$

Given that the mass gained by the cathode is $x \times 10^{-2}\ \text{g}$:

$6.35 = x \times 10^{-2}$

$x = 635$

Answer: $635$

questions.q:
During the electrolysis of acidulated water, oxygen gas is collected at the anode at a steady rate of $11.2 \text{ mL s}^{-1}$ at STP. The constant current passed through the electrolytic cell is ____ A.
(Given: Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP $= 22.4 \text{ L mol}^{-1}$, Faraday constant $F = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
During the electrolysis of acidulated water, oxygen gas is collected at the anode at a steady rate of $11.2 \text{ mL s}^{-1}$ at STP. The constant current passed through the electrolytic cell is ____ A.
(Given: Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP $= 22.4 \text{ L mol}^{-1}$, Faraday constant $F = 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The oxidation reaction at the anode during the electrolysis of acidulated water is:

$2H_2O(l) \rightarrow O_2(g) + 4H^+(aq) + 4e^-$

Volume of $O_2$ produced per second $= 11.2 \text{ mL}$

Moles of $O_2$ produced per second $= \dfrac{11.2}{22400} = \dfrac{1}{2000} \text{ mol}$

From the reaction, $1 \text{ mol}$ of $O_2$ requires the transfer of $4 \text{ mol}$ of electrons. Therefore, the moles of electrons transferred per second is:

$\dfrac{1}{2000} \times 4 = \dfrac{1}{500} \text{ mol}$

Current $I$ is the rate of flow of charge (charge transferred per second):

$I = \text{moles of electrons per second} \times F$

$I = \dfrac{1}{500} \times 96500 = 193 \text{ A}$

Answer: $193$

Sodium amalgam is prepared by the electrolysis of aqueous $\text{NaCl}$ solution using $52.9\text{ g}$ of mercury as the cathode. The amount of electricity required to prepare an amalgam containing $8\%$ sodium by mass, with a current efficiency of $80\%$, is $x \times 10^{-2}\text{ F}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
Sodium amalgam is prepared by the electrolysis of aqueous $\text{NaCl}$ solution using $52.9\text{ g}$ of mercury as the cathode. The amount of electricity required to prepare an amalgam containing $8\%$ sodium by mass, with a current efficiency of $80\%$, is $x \times 10^{-2}\text{ F}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
(Given: Molar mass of $\text{Na} = 23\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Let the mass of sodium deposited in the amalgam be $w$ g.

Total mass of the amalgam = $(w + 52.9)$ g.

Given that the amalgam contains $8\%$ sodium by mass:

$\dfrac{w}{w + 52.9} = \dfrac{8}{100} = 0.08$

$w = 0.08w + 4.232$

$0.92w = 4.232$

$w = 4.6$ g

Number of moles of sodium deposited = $\dfrac{4.6}{23} = 0.2$ mol.

The reduction reaction at the cathode is:

$\text{Na}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Na}$

Theoretical amount of electricity required to deposit $0.2$ mol of Na = $0.2$ F.

Since the current efficiency is $80\%$, the actual amount of electricity required is:

$Q = \dfrac{0.2}{0.80} = 0.25$ F

$Q = 25 \times 10^{-2}$ F

Comparing this with $x \times 10^{-2}$ F, we get $x = 25$.

Answer: $25$

When a certain quantity of electricity is passed through the cells, $11.2\text{ g}$ of metal M and $1.8\text{ g}$ of Al are deposited at the respective cathodes. If the atomic mass of M is $112\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ and that of Al is $27\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, the valency of metal M in its chloride is ____.
questions.question: Two electrolytic cells containing solutions of a chloride of metal M and aluminium chloride ($\text{AlCl}_3$) are connected in series. When a certain quantity of electricity is passed through the cells, $11.2\text{ g}$ of metal M and $1.8\text{ g}$ of Al are deposited at the respective cathodes. If the atomic mass of M is $112\text{ g mol}^{-1}$ and that of Al is $27\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, the valency of metal M in its chloride is ____.
questions.solution:
Moles of Al deposited = $\dfrac{1.8}{27} = \dfrac{1}{15} \text{ mol}$

Valency of Al in $\text{AlCl}_3$ is $3$.

Number of equivalents of Al = Moles of Al $\times$ Valency = $\dfrac{1}{15} \times 3 = 0.2 \text{ eq}$

Since the cells are connected in series, the same quantity of electricity passes through both cells. Therefore, the number of equivalents of metal M deposited is equal to the number of equivalents of Al deposited.

Equivalents of M = $0.2 \text{ eq}$

Moles of M deposited = $\dfrac{11.2}{112} = 0.1 \text{ mol}$

Valency of M = $\dfrac{\text{Equivalents of M}}{\text{Moles of M}} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.1} = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.q:
A constant current is passed through two electrolytic cells connected in series. Cell A contains an aqueous solution of $\text{CuSO}_4$ and cell B contains an aqueous solution of an unknown metal chloride $\text{MCl}_3$. After a certain time, it was found that $1.905\text{ g}$ of copper was deposited at the cathode of cell A and $1.120\text{ g}$ of the unknown metal M was deposited at the cathode of cell B. The molar mass of the metal M is ____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
(Given: Molar mass of Cu is $63.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.question:
A constant current is passed through two electrolytic cells connected in series. Cell A contains an aqueous solution of $\text{CuSO}_4$ and cell B contains an aqueous solution of an unknown metal chloride $\text{MCl}_3$. After a certain time, it was found that $1.905\text{ g}$ of copper was deposited at the cathode of cell A and $1.120\text{ g}$ of the unknown metal M was deposited at the cathode of cell B. The molar mass of the metal M is ____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
(Given: Molar mass of Cu is $63.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's second law of electrolysis, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes connected in series, the masses of the substances deposited are proportional to their equivalent weights.

$\dfrac{W_{\text{Cu}}}{E_{\text{Cu}}} = \dfrac{W_{\text{M}}}{E_{\text{M}}}$

The equivalent weight of copper in $\text{CuSO}_4$ (where Cu is in $+2$ oxidation state) is $E_{\text{Cu}} = \dfrac{63.5}{2} = 31.75 \text{ g eq}^{-1}$.

The equivalent weight of metal M in $\text{MCl}_3$ (where M is in $+3$ oxidation state) is $E_{\text{M}} = \dfrac{M_{\text{M}}}{3}$, where $M_{\text{M}}$ is the molar mass of M.

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1.905}{31.75} = \dfrac{1.120}{E_{\text{M}}}$

$0.06 = \dfrac{1.120}{E_{\text{M}}}$

$E_{\text{M}} = \dfrac{1.120}{0.06} = \dfrac{56}{3} \text{ g eq}^{-1}$

Since $E_{\text{M}} = \dfrac{M_{\text{M}}}{3}$, we get:

$\dfrac{M_{\text{M}}}{3} = \dfrac{56}{3}$

$M_{\text{M}} = 56 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $56$

questions.q: For a given conductivity cell at $298\text{ K}$, which of the following aqueous solutions of $\text{KCl}$ will exhibit the highest electrical resistance?
questions.question: For a given conductivity cell at $298\text{ K}$, which of the following aqueous solutions of $\text{KCl}$ will exhibit the highest electrical resistance?
questions.solution:
The electrical resistance $R$ of a solution in a conductivity cell is given by $R = \rho \dfrac{l}{A} = \dfrac{1}{\kappa} \dfrac{l}{A}$, where $\kappa$ is the conductivity and $\dfrac{l}{A}$ is the cell constant.

For a given conductivity cell, the cell constant is fixed, which implies $R \propto \dfrac{1}{\kappa}$.

Conductivity $\kappa$ is defined as the conductance of a unit volume of solution. It depends directly on the number of ions present per unit volume. As the concentration of the electrolyte decreases, the number of ions per unit volume decreases, resulting in a lower conductivity $\kappa$.

Since resistance is inversely proportional to conductivity, the solution with the lowest concentration will have the lowest conductivity and consequently the highest electrical resistance.

Among the given options, $0.01\text{ M}$ is the lowest concentration. Thus, the $0.01\text{ M}$ $\text{KCl}$ solution will exhibit the highest electrical resistance.

Answer: $0.01\text{ M}$

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the effect of temperature on the molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of an electrolytic solution?
questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the effect of temperature on the molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of an electrolytic solution?
options: $\Lambda_m$ decreases with an increase in temperature for both strong and weak electrolytes.
$\Lambda_m$ is independent of temperature as the total number of moles of electrolyte remains constant.
$\Lambda_m$ increases with an increase in temperature for both strong and weak electrolytes.
$\Lambda_m$ increases for strong electrolytes but decreases for weak electrolytes with an increase in temperature.
questions.solution:
The molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of an electrolytic solution depends on the mobility of ions and the number of ions present in the solution.

With an increase in temperature, the kinetic energy of the ions increases and the viscosity of the solvent decreases. This results in an increase in the mobility of the ions.

For weak electrolytes, an increase in temperature also increases the degree of dissociation, thereby increasing the number of ions in the solution.

For strong electrolytes, although they are completely dissociated, the increased ionic mobility leads to higher conductivity.

Therefore, $\Lambda_m$ increases with an increase in temperature for both strong and weak electrolytes.

Answer: $\Lambda_m$ increases with an increase in temperature for both strong and weak electrolytes.

questions.q: Among the following pure substances, which one will not conduct electricity in its liquid state?
questions.question: Among the following pure substances, which one will not conduct electricity in its liquid state?
questions.solution:
Liquefied $\text{HBr}$ is a polar covalent compound. In its pure liquid state, it exists as discrete molecules and does not auto-ionize to produce free ions. Since there are no free ions or mobile electrons available, it does not conduct electricity.

Molten $\text{NaOH}$ and molten $\text{CaCl}_2$ are ionic compounds. In their molten states, the electrostatic forces of attraction are overcome, freeing the ions ($\text{Na}^+$, $\text{OH}^-$, $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{Cl}^-$) to move and conduct electricity.

Liquid $\text{Ga}$ is a metal and conducts electricity due to the presence of free, delocalized valence electrons.

Answer: Liquefied $\text{HBr}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of limiting molar conductivities ($\Lambda_m^\circ$) for the following alkali metal chlorides in aqueous solution is :
questions.question: The correct order of limiting molar conductivities ($\Lambda_m^\circ$) for the following alkali metal chlorides in aqueous solution is :
questions.solution:
The limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte in aqueous solution depends on the ionic mobility of its constituent ions.

Since the chloride ion ($\text{Cl}^{-}$) is common to all the given salts, the conductivity depends on the alkali metal cations: $\text{Li}^{+}$, $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{K}^{+}$, and $\text{Rb}^{+}$.

The size of the bare cations increases down the group: $\text{Li}^{+} < \text{Na}^{+} < \text{K}^{+} < \text{Rb}^{+}$.

Smaller cations have a higher charge density and undergo more extensive hydration in aqueous solution. Therefore, the size of the hydrated cations follows the reverse order: $\text{Li}^{+}(\text{aq}) > \text{Na}^{+}(\text{aq}) > \text{K}^{+}(\text{aq}) > \text{Rb}^{+}(\text{aq})$.

A larger hydrated ion experiences greater resistance to movement in solution, resulting in lower ionic mobility. Thus, the ionic mobility and the limiting molar conductivity follow the order: $\text{Rb}^{+} > \text{K}^{+} > \text{Na}^{+} > \text{Li}^{+}$.

Consequently, the correct order of limiting molar conductivities for the alkali metal chlorides is $\text{RbCl} > \text{KCl} > \text{NaCl} > \text{LiCl}$.

Answer: $\text{RbCl} > \text{KCl} > \text{NaCl} > \text{LiCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: As the concentration of an aqueous solution of a strong electrolyte approaches zero, its molar conductivity:
questions.question: As the concentration of an aqueous solution of a strong electrolyte approaches zero, its molar conductivity:
options: approaches a finite limiting value which is less than its value at higher concentrations.
approaches a finite limiting value which is greater than its value at higher concentrations.
remains constant since strong electrolytes are completely ionized at all concentrations.
approaches zero due to the decrease in the number of ions per unit volume.
questions.solution:
For a strong electrolyte, the variation of molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ with concentration $c$ is given by the Debye-Huckel-Onsager equation:

$\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt{c}$

where $\Lambda_m^\circ$ is the limiting molar conductivity (molar conductivity at infinite dilution) and $A$ is a constant depending on the nature of the solvent and temperature.

As the concentration $c$ approaches zero, the term $A\sqrt{c}$ approaches zero. Thus, $\Lambda_m$ approaches $\Lambda_m^\circ$, which is a maximum finite limiting value.

At higher concentrations, interionic attractions (such as electrophoretic and relaxation effects) retard the motion of ions, resulting in a lower molar conductivity. Therefore, as concentration approaches zero, the molar conductivity approaches a finite limiting value which is greater than its value at higher concentrations.

Answer: approaches a finite limiting value which is greater than its value at higher concentrations.

questions.q: Which of the following $0.1\text{ M}$ aqueous solutions will exhibit the highest electrical conductivity at $298\text{ K}$?
questions.question: Which of the following $0.1\text{ M}$ aqueous solutions will exhibit the highest electrical conductivity at $298\text{ K}$?
questions.solution:
Electrical conductivity of an aqueous solution depends on the number of ions present in the solution and their ionic mobility.

$\text{H}_3\text{BO}_3$ and $\text{HCOOH}$ are weak acids and dissociate only partially in water, resulting in a low concentration of ions.

$\text{HCl}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ are strong acids and dissociate completely in water.

$\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{H}^+ + \text{Cl}^-$ (Yields $2$ moles of ions per mole of acid)

$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2\text{H}^+ + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$ (Yields $3$ moles of ions per mole of acid)

Since $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ produces the maximum number of ions ($0.3\text{ M}$ total ions) compared to $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$ ($0.2\text{ M}$ total ions), it will exhibit the highest electrical conductivity.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$

$\Lambda^{\circ}_{m}(\text{SrSO}_4) = \lambda^{\circ}(\text{Sr}^{2+}) + \lambda^{\circ}(\text{SO}_{4}^{2-})$

$\Lambda^{\circ}_{m}(\text{SrSO}_4) = 118.0 + 162.0 = 280.0 \text{ S cm}^{2} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

The relationship between molar conductivity, specific conductance $\kappa$, and solubility $S$ (in $\text{mol L}^{-1}$) is:

$\Lambda_{m} = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{S}$

Substituting the given values:

$280.0 = \dfrac{7.0 \times 10^{-5} \times 1000}{S}$

$S = \dfrac{7.0 \times 10^{-2}}{280.0}$

$S = 25 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

Comparing this with $x \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, the value of $x$ is $25$.

Answer: $25$

Percentage dissociation = $\alpha \times 100 = 0.03 \times 100 = 3$

$C = 0.2 \ \text{mol L}^{-1} = 0.2 \times 10^3 \ \text{mol m}^{-3} = 200 \ \text{mol m}^{-3}$

Comparing this with the given value $x \times 10^{-4} \ \Omega^{-1} \ \text{m}^2 \ \text{mol}^{-1}$, we get:

Answer: $15$

questions.q: An aqueous solution of $\text{MgSO}_4$ is titrated conductometrically by gradually adding an aqueous solution of $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ from a burette. Which of the following best describes the variation in the electrical conductivity of the mixture as the titrant is added in excess?
questions.question: An aqueous solution of $\text{MgSO}_4$ is titrated conductometrically by gradually adding an aqueous solution of $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ from a burette. Which of the following best describes the variation in the electrical conductivity of the mixture as the titrant is added in excess?
options: It increases initially to a maximum and then decreases.
It decreases initially to a minimum and then increases.
questions.solution:
The chemical reaction involved in the titration is:

$\text{MgSO}_4(aq) + \text{Ba(OH)}_2(aq) \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(s) \downarrow + \text{Mg(OH)}_2(s) \downarrow$

Initially, the conductivity of the solution is due to the presence of $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ ions. As $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is added, both the products formed, $\text{BaSO}_4$ and $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, are highly insoluble and precipitate out of the solution. This removes the conducting ions from the aqueous phase, causing the electrical conductivity to decrease continuously until the equivalence point is reached, where it becomes minimum.

When excess $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is added beyond the equivalence point, it does not react further and remains in the solution as $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ and $\text{OH}^-$ ions. The addition of these ions, especially the highly mobile $\text{OH}^-$ ions, causes the electrical conductivity of the mixture to increase.

Therefore, the conductivity decreases initially to a minimum and then increases.

Answer: It decreases initially to a minimum and then increases.

$C = \dfrac{\kappa}{\Lambda^\circ_m}$

Substituting the given values:

Converting the concentration from $\text{mol m}^{-3}$ to $\text{mol L}^{-1}$ (since $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1000 \text{ L}$):

$C = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-4}}{1000} \text{ mol L}^{-1} = 3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

In pure water, $[\text{H}^+] = [\text{OH}^-] = C = 3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ mol L}^{-1}$.

The ionic product of water ($K_w$) is:

$K_w = [\text{H}^+][\text{OH}^-] = (3 \times 10^{-7})^2 = 9 \times 10^{-14} \text{ mol}^2 \text{ L}^{-2}$

Comparing this with $x \times 10^{-14} \text{ mol}^2 \text{ L}^{-2}$, we get $x = 9$.

$K_a = \dfrac{0.049 \times 0.0004}{0.98}$

$K_a = \dfrac{1}{20} \times 4 \times 10^{-4}$

$K_a = 2 \times 10^{-5}$

Comparing this with $x \times 10^{-5}$, the value of $x$ is $2$.

Answer: $2$

$\text{NaOH}(\text{aq})$$0.020 \text{ M}$$100 \text{ mL}$

Assume the volumes are additive. The conductivity ($\kappa$) of the resulting solution is $8.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$. The molar conductivity of the resulting mixture is ________ $\text{S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)

SolutionMolarityVolume

Assume the volumes are additive. The conductivity ($\kappa$) of the resulting solution is $8.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ S cm}^{-1}$. The molar conductivity of the resulting mixture is ________ $\text{S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
The reaction between acetic acid and sodium hydroxide is given by:

$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Millimoles of $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} = 0.020 \text{ M} \times 100 \text{ mL} = 2 \text{ mmol}$

Millimoles of $\text{NaOH} = 0.020 \text{ M} \times 100 \text{ mL} = 2 \text{ mmol}$

Since both reactants are present in equal amounts, they completely neutralize each other to form $2 \text{ mmol}$ of $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$.

Total volume of the resulting mixture $= 100 \text{ mL} + 100 \text{ mL} = 200 \text{ mL}$

Concentration of $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ in the resulting solution ($C$) $= \dfrac{2 \text{ mmol}}{200 \text{ mL}} = 0.010 \text{ M}$

The molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) is calculated using the formula:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{C}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{8.4 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{0.010}$

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{0.84}{0.010} = 84 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $84$

questions.q:
The molar conductivities ($\Lambda_m$) of an aqueous solution of a strong electrolyte $AB_2$ at $298 \text{ K}$ and at different concentrations ($c$) are given below:
Concentration ($c$) / $\text{mol L}^{-1}$$\Lambda_m$ / $\Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$
$0.01$$264$
$0.04$$258$

By using Kohlrausch's empirical equation for strong electrolytes, the limiting molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m^\infty$) of $AB_2$ is ____ $\Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.question:
The molar conductivities ($\Lambda_m$) of an aqueous solution of a strong electrolyte $AB_2$ at $298 \text{ K}$ and at different concentrations ($c$) are given below:
Concentration ($c$) / $\text{mol L}^{-1}$$\Lambda_m$ / $\Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$
$0.01$$264$
$0.04$$258$

By using Kohlrausch's empirical equation for strong electrolytes, the limiting molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m^\infty$) of $AB_2$ is ____ $\Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
According to Kohlrausch's empirical equation for strong electrolytes:

$\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\infty - b\sqrt{c}$

Substituting the given values for the two concentrations:

$264 = \Lambda_m^\infty - b\sqrt{0.01}$

$264 = \Lambda_m^\infty - 0.1b$

And for the second concentration:

$258 = \Lambda_m^\infty - b\sqrt{0.04}$

$258 = \Lambda_m^\infty - 0.2b$

Subtracting the second equation from the first equation:

$264 - 258 = 0.2b - 0.1b$

$6 = 0.1b \Rightarrow b = 60$

Substituting the value of $b$ in the first equation:

$264 = \Lambda_m^\infty - 0.1 \times 60$

$264 = \Lambda_m^\infty - 6$

$\Lambda_m^\infty = 270$

Answer: $270$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The resistance of a conductivity cell when filled with an aqueous solution P is $50$ $\Omega$. When the same cell is filled with an aqueous solution Q, its resistance is $100$ $\Omega$. If equal volumes of solutions P and Q are mixed, the resistance of the resulting mixture measured in the same cell is ____ $\Omega$. (Nearest integer)
(Assume that there is no change in the degree of dissociation of P and Q upon mixing and no chemical reaction occurs between them.)
questions.question:
The resistance of a conductivity cell when filled with an aqueous solution P is $50$ $\Omega$. When the same cell is filled with an aqueous solution Q, its resistance is $100$ $\Omega$. If equal volumes of solutions P and Q are mixed, the resistance of the resulting mixture measured in the same cell is ____ $\Omega$. (Nearest integer)
(Assume that there is no change in the degree of dissociation of P and Q upon mixing and no chemical reaction occurs between them.)
questions.solution:
Let the cell constant be $G^*$.

Conductivity of solution P, $\kappa_P = \dfrac{G^*}{R_P} = \dfrac{G^*}{50}$

Conductivity of solution Q, $\kappa_Q = \dfrac{G^*}{R_Q} = \dfrac{G^*}{100}$

When equal volumes of solutions P and Q are mixed, the concentration of ions from each solution is halved. Since there is no change in the degree of dissociation, the conductivity of the mixture is the average of their individual conductivities.

$\kappa_{mix} = \dfrac{\kappa_P + \kappa_Q}{2}$

$\kappa_{mix} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{G^*}{50} + \dfrac{G^*}{100} \right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{3G^*}{100} \right) = \dfrac{3G^*}{200}$

The resistance of the mixture is given by:

$R_{mix} = \dfrac{G^*}{\kappa_{mix}} = \dfrac{G^*}{\dfrac{3G^*}{200}} = \dfrac{200}{3}$

$R_{mix} = 66.67$ $\Omega$

Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get $67$.

Answer: $67$

questions.q: In a conductivity cell, two platinum electrodes, each having an area of $8 \text{ cm}^2$, are placed $1.2 \text{ cm}$ apart. The cell is filled with a $0.025 \text{ M}$ solution of a salt. If the electrodes are exactly half-dipped into the solution and the resistance of the cell is $100 \, \Omega$, the molar conductivity of the salt solution is ________ $\Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.question: In a conductivity cell, two platinum electrodes, each having an area of $8 \text{ cm}^2$, are placed $1.2 \text{ cm}$ apart. The cell is filled with a $0.025 \text{ M}$ solution of a salt. If the electrodes are exactly half-dipped into the solution and the resistance of the cell is $100 \, \Omega$, the molar conductivity of the salt solution is ________ $\Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
Since the electrodes are exactly half-dipped into the solution, the effective area of the electrodes in contact with the electrolyte is half of the total area.

Effective area, $A_{\text{eff}} = \dfrac{8}{2} = 4 \text{ cm}^2$

Distance between the electrodes, $l = 1.2 \text{ cm}$

Cell constant, $G^* = \dfrac{l}{A_{\text{eff}}} = \dfrac{1.2}{4} = 0.3 \text{ cm}^{-1}$

Conductivity, $\kappa = \dfrac{G^*}{R} = \dfrac{0.3}{100} = 3 \times 10^{-3} \, \Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^{-1}$

Molar conductivity is given by:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa \times 1000}{C}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-3} \times 1000}{0.025} = \dfrac{3}{0.025} = 120 \, \Omega^{-1} \text{ cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $120$
